title: Bootstrapped Mumbai pizza brand Hundo Pizza raises Rs 7.5 crore in first institutional funding
summary: Hundo Pizza raises 7.5 crore rupees in maiden institutional funding led by Titan Capital
detailed: Mumbai-based delivery-first pizza brand Hundo Pizza raised Rs 7.5 crore in its first institutional funding round led by Titan Capital.

Additional participants in the round included Indian Silicon Valley Capital (ISVC), Ankur Rangnekar, Akshay Rangnekar, and angel investor Haresh Chawla, with Wavelength Partners acting as deal advisor.
The bootstrapped startup closed FY26 with Rs 18 crore in revenue, operates at an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 35 crore, and targets Rs 60 crore in FY28.
Funds will be used to expand across Mumbai, enter a new city, and build a 5,000 sq ft fully electric central kitchen and production facility in Andheri East.
sentences: Mumbai-based delivery-first pizza brand Hundo Pizza has raised Rs 7.5 crore in its first institutional funding round led by Titan Capital, the investment firm founded by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal.
Indian Silicon Valley Capital (ISVC), Ankur Rangnekar, Akshay Rangnekar and angel investor Haresh Chawla also took part in the round, the startup said.
Wavelength Partners acted as the deal advisor.
It will use the fresh capital to expand across Mumbai, enter a new city and strengthen its production infrastructure.
It is targeting an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 60 crore in FY28.
Hundo Pizza closed FY26 with revenue of Rs 18 crore and said it currently operates at an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 35 crore.
That run rate is nearly double its FY26 revenue, and the FY28 target would mean growing it by roughly 71% from current levels.
Hundo Pizza has largely operated as a bootstrapped business.
Before its latest institutional funding round, the brand raised approximately $40,100 in February 2022 from two individual investors, according to Tracxn.
As part of the expansion, Hundo Pizza is building a 5,000 sq ft central kitchen and production facility in Andheri East.
It said the facility will be fully electric and will support its production needs as it opens more outlets.
Over the next 12 months, it plans to invest in production capacity, technology and organisational capabilities.
It is also exploring other revenue channels, including events and catering.
Founded in 2020 by Kabir Moorjani and Ronak Rajani, Hundo Pizza began operations in August that year in Mumbai’s Bandra West, initially offering delivery and drive-through services.
The brand specialises in Neo-Neapolitan-style pizzas prepared using ingredients such as San Marzano tomatoes and fresh buffalo mozzarella.
Moorjani serves as Hundo Pizza’s co-founder and chef.
He trained at Les Roches International School of Hotel Management and Le Cordon Bleu Paris and previously founded the Thai restaurant Aroi Mumbai.
Rajani leads growth and marketing.
He founded Mumbai Foodie, a food discovery platform that Swiggy acquired in 2024.
Hundo operates in a category dominated by large chains.
Domino's India, run by Jubilant FoodWorks, had 2,513 outlets as of June 2026, while Pizza Hut's two Indian operators, Devyani and Sapphire, together ran 987, according to media reports.
India's overall pizza market was valued at $5.44 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach $9.33 billion by 2031, growing at an annual rate of about 9.46%, according to TechSci Research.
